Figure 2. Overview of 3D Gaussian Splatting Training Pipeline.

summary: GS-Scale is a memory-efficient training system for large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting that keeps all Gaussians in host memory and transfers only a working subset to the GPU per pass. This figure is a background illustration (not GS-Scale's own architecture) of the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting training pipeline that GS-Scale must accelerate. It shows, left to right, Gaussians initialized from an SfM point cloud, viewed from a camera viewpoint as 3D Gaussians, projected into 2D Gaussians, sorted by depth, and rasterized into a rendered image. The rendered image is compared to a ground-truth image to compute a loss, whose gradients propagate back to update Gaussian parameters and periodically densify the Gaussian set, closing the loop. Seven circled numbers mark the ordered steps: projection, sorting, rendering, loss computation, gradient propagation, parameter update, and periodic densification.
